title: AI for Fraud Detection in NGO Operations: Bringing Trust with Data-Driven Governance
summary: Two independent researchers propose a three-tier AI framework that verifies NGO registrations, monitors transactions and prioritizes audits; its 30% fraud reduction is a projection.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Shivang Rattan and Swapnil Morande, who describe themselves as independent researchers, propose a three-tier AI framework for automated NGO verification, transaction monitoring and audits. They planned a proof of concept on synthetic data modeled on the NGO Darpan registry. They also planned a pilot with 50 NGOs in Maharashtra in the third quarter of 2025. The team projected that the system would reduce fraudulent transactions by 30% within 12 months of pilot deployment. The team also expected that automation would decrease audit processing time by 50%. No result from that pilot has been published, so the fraud and audit-efficiency improvements remain projections.
